summary: Same pattern — both sides fire one full-width icicle band every ~6 s that descends the strip and fades — but the port never draws the original's deep alternating-column comb and picks its hues from a narrow blue-dominated range instead of the whole wheel.
observations: Default rig is grid 16x16 (256 px); the pattern is index-driven, so a 'band' is a contiguous run of pixel indices that fills whole rows. Both sides render without compile or runtime errors, neither binds sensors, and neither exposes any controls (meta.json sides.*.controls == [] on both).
Event cadence matches: over 90 s at 20 fps both sides fire 13 discrete icicle events, one at a time, never overlapping (orig 13, port 13 at seed 1; 14/13 at seed 7; 12/13 at seed 1234).

Motion matches: on both sides the band starts at row 0 and translates monotonically downward to the far end. Mean descent speed (centroid tracked from --dump at 0.5 s spacing, averaged over all events) is orig 4.04 rows/s vs port 3.51 rows/s at 20 fps — overlapping distributions (orig 2.9-5.8, port 1.8-5.5), port ~13% slower on average.
Neither side is frame-rate coupled: centroid speed measured at 10/20/40 fps is orig 3.85 / 4.04 / 4.30 rows/s and port 3.89 / 3.51 / 3.84 rows/s — no scaling with fps on either side.

Band thickness matches: mean 2.0-4.1 lit rows out of 16 on both sides. Brightness profile along the band matches too — median profile skew (over all lit frames) is orig -0.63/-0.32/-0.62 and port -0.57/-0.50/-0.44 for seeds 1/7/1234, i.e. both taper the same way (brightest at the leading lower edge, dim tail trailing above).

COLOUR DISTRIBUTION DIVERGES. Median hue per event over three seeds (30 coloured orig events, 28 coloured port events): the original spreads across the wheel — warm/orange 20-56 deg (~33%), green 117-144 (~10%), cyan 185-192 (~13%), blue 217-253 (~30%), magenta/violet 297-357 (~13%). The port is 21 of 28 events in 215-240 deg blue (~75%), with 5 warm (21-36), one green (144), one violet (288), and NO cyan at all.

TEXTURE DIVERGES. Both sides draw the same regular alternating-column comb when they texture a band (row autocorrelation at lag 1 = -1.00, lag 2 = +1.00 on both), but the comb depth differs. Classifying each event by its peak parity contrast |even-odd|/(even+odd): original produces deep-comb events (>0.35) on 7/13, 7/14 and 2/12 events for seeds 1/7/1234 (16 of 39 total); the port produces ZERO deep-comb events in all 39 events across the same three seeds, only flat bands or shallow combs (<0.35).

Consequence of the above, measured on two-tone rows: the dim column's luminance relative to the bright column is orig 0.21/0.21/0.18 (median, seeds 1/7/1234) but port 0.67/0.67/0.65 — the original's alternate column is ~5x dimmer (reads as a dashed/striped icicle), the port's only ~1.5x dimmer (reads as a near-solid bar).

Concrete example frames (--dump, seed 1, 20 fps): at t=20 s the original's band rows 1-4 alternate (98,98,98) white with (70,0,73) magenta; at t=35 s (99,99,99) white with (4,80,0) green. The port's comparable mixed events are e.g. t=24.5 s (65,65,65) white with (0,37,93) blue and t=82 s (58,58,58) with (0,49,195) blue — same construction, weaker contrast, always blue.

Fraction of perfectly uniform (single-colour) lit rows: orig 30/29/41% vs port 61/74/62% for seeds 1/7/1234. Rows with more than two distinct colours: orig 21-39%, port 8-21%. The port's bands are flat far more often.
Event mix by texture family is otherwise similar: both sides produce all-white events (orig 2/13, 3/14, 4/12; port 3/13, 5/13, 3/13), pure-hue events, and half-white/half-hue comb events.

Events last longer on the port: mean event duration 2.9-3.1 s (orig) vs 3.7-4.0 s (port), consistently at 10, 20 and 40 fps. The original's icicle usually fades out before reaching the far end (centroid travel often stops at row 9.5-13); the port's more often carries to row 14-15.

As a result the port is brighter over a long window even though per-event peaks match: mean frame luminance orig 3.1/4.9/4.2 vs port 4.3/7.5/9.8 (seeds 1/7/1234), and lit pixels per frame orig 18.7/20.4/23.5 vs port 27.9/30.1/30.3. Median per-event peak luminance is comparable (orig 8.2/17.4/11.8, port 11.0/13.9/11.6).

Rig-scaling behaviour matches: re-rendered on a 32x32 / 1024 px grid both sides still draw a single band whose thickness is the same fraction of the strip (~1/6), so both are pixel-count-relative rather than fixed-canvas.

The untouched-default 6 s baseline window is unrepresentative and misleading on its own: it lands on a bright green/white orig event (mean brightness 7) against a dim uniform-blue port event (mean 2). Over 90 s the two sides' brightness ordering reverses. No conclusion should be drawn from the default 6 s window on this pattern.
feedback: Motion, cadence, band width, taper direction and rig-scaling are already right — do not touch them. Event rate (~13 per 90 s), descent speed (~4 rows/s on a 16x16 grid = ~64 px/s of strip) and the downward direction all match the original within event-to-event randomness.

Main fix 1 — hue selection. The original picks each icicle's hue roughly uniformly around the wheel: across 30 events it produced orange/red (~33%), green (~10%), cyan (~13%), blue (~30%) and magenta/violet (~13%). The port produced blue (215-240 deg) on 75% of 28 events and never once produced cyan. Widen the per-event hue draw to cover the full circle instead of clustering near blue; a correct port should show cyan and magenta icicles roughly as often as blue ones.

Main fix 2 — comb contrast. Both sides already alternate colour by pixel-index parity, so the mechanism is present; the port's two interleaved tones are simply too close in brightness. On the original the dim column sits at ~0.20 of the bright column's luminance (median over three seeds), and about 40% of events use that deep contrast so the icicle reads as a dashed/striped bar. On the port the dim column is at ~0.66 and no event in 39 sampled ever went below 0.35, so every band reads as a near-solid bar. Push the dim tone down to roughly a fifth of the bright tone on the events that use the comb.

Secondary — the port's icicle lingers ~25-30% longer than the original's (mean event duration 3.8 s vs 3.0 s) and more often survives all the way to the far end of the strip, where the original's typically fades out around 60-85% of the way down. Speed up the fade/decay so events die earlier; this also fixes the port's ~1.4-2.3x higher long-window mean brightness (27.9-30.3 lit pixels per frame vs the original's 18.7-23.5), which is caused by the longer-lived bands rather than by any per-event peak being too bright — per-event peak luminance already matches.

Do not use the default 6 s window to check any of this: at seed 1 it happens to show a bright green original against a dim blue port, which exaggerates a brightness gap that reverses over 90 s. Verify against >=90 s at 20 fps and at least three well-separated seeds (1, 7, 1234), scoring per-event hue and per-event parity contrast.
